text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Tuesday.

LONDON - Leading shares soared to their highest-ever levels amid euphoria over the new British government's decision to grant the Bank of England freedom to set interest rates without political interference.

Labour's new Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown's decision to grant the BoE a level of independence was well received by market professionals, still uncertain about how tough a party last in power 18 years ago, would be on inflation and monetary policy.
The FTSE 100 Index closed 63.7 points higher to a record closing level of 4,519.3.
FRANKFURT - The German share market ended bourse trade at a record closing high, powered ahead by record overnight gains in the U.S. and Japan and well-received results from top companies.

After setting a new session high of 3,584.56 points in earlx trade, the blue chip DAX index pared its gains to close at 3,568.28, up 39.50 points, or 1.12 percent. In post-bourse trade the DAX stood at 3548.52 down 17.17 points.
PARIS - French stocks fell on polls suggesting a close parliamentary election between the ruling conservatives and the Socialists.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 20.91 points or 0.78 percent at 2,651.93 after losing its early gains triggered by a sharp rise on Wall Street on Monday.

ZURICH - Swiss shares broke from their recent record run to end below the 5,000 point-level in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) after Nestle's first quarter results triggered profit taking on a broad front.
"The correction is only normal after the recent strong rise," one dealer said.
The SMI slipped 41.2 points, or 0.82 percent, to end at 4,988.4 and the broad Swiss Performance Index dropped 19.74 points, or 0.62 percent, to 3,150.82.

TOKYO - The Tokyo stock market returned from a long holiday weekend in a bullish mood, with the benchmark index powering above the closely watched 20,000 point barrier for the first time since mid-December.
Brokers said a buying binge by foreign investors combined with pension fund purchases to fuel a hefty gain of over three percent.
The 225-share Nikkei average jumped 666.17 points or 3.41 percent to finish at 20,180.92, the highest closing level since 20,413.46 set on December 17.
HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks continued their powerful advance for the fifth day in a row on Tuesday, closing on hefty gains as Monday's record highs on Wall Street swept local prices higher.
The Hang Seng Index jumped 180.00 points, or 1.34 percent, to 13,579.34. The index hit an intra-day high of 13,679.92, the first time it has been above 13,600 points since late February.
SYDNEY - Australian stocks closed at a record high after a fresh high on Wall Street and strong rises in other markets in the Asia Pacific region encouraged investors.
The All Ordinaries index ended 20.1 points higher at 2,512.8 after earlier hitting a new intra-day high of 2,518.5 with A$962.41 million (US$750.68 million) worth of trade going through the market.
JOHANNESBURG - South Africa's all-share index rose to a record closing high on Tuesday despite industrial shares being knocked off their highs by expectations of a weaker Wall Street opening.

Gold shares ended slightly firmer after bullion gained three dollars on Monday. But dealers said volumes were thin and players were concerned that the rise in the bullion price could not be sustained.
The all-share index 21.6 points stronger to a new high of 7,212.0 points, the industrial index was up 5.3 points to 8,568.7 points and the gold index added 6.6 points to 1,212.3 points.
